title: House interiors: real floor, interior wall finish and ceiling (not bare brick)
description: Noted after first walk-through (2026-09-23): inside house_peaked the floor is the 5 cm brick slab left by the interior cutter and the inside wall faces are the same exterior brick; there is no ceiling, so the roof underside shows. Buildings need an interior finish separate from the exterior: a floor part (e.g. hardwood_floor) at floor level, an interior wall lining (plaster/paint) distinct from the exterior brick, and a ceiling at wall_height. Options: lining parts generated from the interior cutter volume, or per-face material groups (geogen-o3s.22). Should reuse the interior material pack (3cc.5) and finishes work (3cc.3), and fit the floor plan model (3cc.1) so hotel rooms get the same treatment. Window and door openings must cut through the lining too.

title: Interactable doors: open/close the cottage front door in Godot
description: Noted after first walk-through (2026-09-23): the cottage door is a solid closed leaf, so the house can't be entered. Vertical slice ahead of the full interaction system (3cc.19/3cc.28): door.yaml declares its leaf as openable (hinge side + axis at the jamb, open angle, swing direction), export writes it into extras.geogen on the leaf node, and the Godot runtime animates the leaf about the hinge when the player looks at it within reach and presses E (prompt label). The leaf's collider must move with it (AnimatableBody3D) so an open door lets the player through and a closed one blocks. 3cc.28 should generalise this rather than replace it.
acceptance_criteria: In Godot, walk up to the cottage door, press E, it swings open on its hinge, walk inside; press E again to close. Headless walk test: closed door blocks, open door lets the player into the house.

title: Godot 4 project scaffold in runtime/godot (empty, boots headless)
description: Carve-out of geogen-3cc.26: bring up an empty Godot 4.7 project at runtime/godot/ (Forward+, 1 unit = 1 m) with a main scene (sun, environment, ground plane, camera), a generated/ folder for exports, .gitignore for .godot/, and a README pinning the Godot version and documenting how to launch from the CLI. No player/loader yet.
acceptance_criteria: 'godot --path runtime/godot' opens the project; headless run of the main scene exits cleanly; a screenshot of the main scene looks correct
close_reason: Empty Godot 4.7 project at runtime/godot boots headless and renders main scene (screenshot verified)

title: Godot import plugin: extras.geogen -> Areas, spawns, groups, navigation
description: EditorScenePostImport / GLTFDocumentExtension in runtime/godot/addons/geogen/: read node metadata from extras.geogen and build runtime nodes: room_volume -> Area3D with room id/type (player 'current room'), spawn -> Marker3D in group 'geogen_spawn', tags -> node groups, walkable/navmesh nodes -> NavigationRegion3D (bake at import or load), collider hints the suffix convention can't express. Validates schema version and warns on unknown components.
notes: From 3cc.26: overlay shows 'room: -' placeholder and has no navmesh toggle yet; wire both up here once rooms/navmesh come through extras.geogen. WorldLoader._add_collision currently adds trimesh colliders to every mesh; switch to exported -col/-colonly colliders when 3cc.17 lands.

title: Godot runtime project + first-person player + hot-reload loop
description: runtime/godot/: Godot 4.x project (pinned version in README, Forward+, 1 unit = 1 m). Player: CharacterBody3D first-person controller (mouse look, WASD, jump, crouch optional, step-up) sized from the export manifest's player spec; spawn at a geogen spawn point or scene origin. World loader scene that instances every .glb in res://generated/ (or the one named on the command line). Dev loop: 'python -m geogen.main -s cottage --export-godot' writes .glb + manifest into runtime/godot/generated/, the Godot editor reimports on change; 'godot --path runtime/godot -- --scene cottage' runs straight into walk mode. Debug overlay: FPS, current room tag, toggle colliders/navmesh display.
acceptance_criteria: Export the cottage, launch Godot from the CLI, and walk around it with collision
close_reason: --export-godot writes glb+manifest to runtime/godot/generated; runtime loads exports via GLTFDocument with trimesh colliders + mipmaps, hot-reloads on manifest change; cylinder first-person Player sized from PlayerSpec with step-up; overlay (FPS, pos, room placeholder), F2 collider wireframes, F3 fly, F4 overview. Headless walk tests: wall blocks, 0.3 m door step climbed, closed leaf blocks. Navmesh display + room tags deferred to 3cc.27 (no navmesh/rooms exported yet).

title: Shared player spec (player.yaml) for generation and runtime
description: Single source of truth for player-scale constraints: assets/player.yaml with capsule radius (0.3 m), height (1.8 m), eye height (1.65 m), step height (0.3 m), max walkable slope (40 deg), min door clear opening (0.85 x 2.0 m), min corridor width (1.2 m), interaction reach (1.5 m). Loaded by a geogen.player module; used by layout validation/navigability (3cc.8), stairs and door generators as defaults, written into the export manifest, and read by the Godot player controller so 'enterable' means the same on both sides.
acceptance_criteria: player.yaml loaded via geogen.player; manifest contains it; Godot controller reads capsule/step/slope from the manifest
close_reason: assets/player.yaml + geogen.player (validated PlayerSpec); glTF exports write <name>.manifest.json with the player spec; Godot PlayerSpec reads it (round-trip test with non-default values). Wiring into the CharacterBody3D controller lands with 3cc.26.

title: Runtime: Godot 4 is the reference player
description:
Decision: Godot 4 (pinned 4.x release) is geogen's reference runtime/player. geogen stays engine-agnostic; the contract is glTF + versioned extras.geogen schema + JSON sidecar/manifest.

Why: Godot provides what M2-M4 need (CharacterBody3D, physics, navmesh, clustered many-light rendering, LOD/occlusion, streaming) instead of us building a mini engine; its glTF importer natively maps node-name suffixes (-col, -colonly, -convcolonly, -navmesh) to colliders/navmeshes and imports extras as node metadata; post-import scripts can map interaction components to behaviours; MIT licensed, headless CLI for CI, reimports changed files for a hot-reload loop; and it is an engine target game devs can actually keep building on.

Alternatives: Three.js (great for shareable web preview, but we'd build controller/physics/nav/lighting/streaming ourselves) -> kept as a later preview runtime to prove schema portability. Unity (large user base, but closed and extras import needs custom glTFast code) -> later importer target.

Consequences: Qt viewer remains the generator inspector (validation, UV checker, cutaway); walking and interaction live in Godot. Player dimensions are defined once in geogen and shared by generator validation and the Godot controller.

title: Gameplay metadata in export: extras.geogen schema, Godot-compatible colliders, rooms, spawns
description: Make exports game-ready: semantic tags on every node (room.hotel_bedroom, furniture.bed, door.interior), auto-generated collision geometry (simplified boxes/convex hulls per part, walls as boxes; override with collider: none|box|hull|mesh in YAML), walkable-surface flags, room/trigger volumes, spawn points and anchors. Written to glTF node extras plus a JSON sidecar with a documented schema.
design: Colliders use Godot's glTF import suffixes so they work with zero plugin code: '<part>-colonly' (box/convex collider only), '-convcolonly', '-col' (trimesh + visual) and '-navmesh' for walkable floors; YAML collider: none|box|hull|mesh|auto per part (auto = box for cube-like parts, convex hull otherwise, walls as boxes). Node extras: extras.geogen = {version: 1, tags: [...], collider: ..., room: {id, type}, interactions: {...}}; room volumes and spawn points as empty nodes with extras (type: room_volume / spawn). JSON Schema at docs/schema/geogen-extras.v1.schema.json, validated in tests. Export manifest (JSON sidecar) lists chunks, player spec, rooms, spawns and schema version.

title: Multi-storey building generator: storeys, slabs, stair and elevator cores
description: Building = footprint + stacked floor plans. Floor slabs with thickness, repeated typical floors with per-floor overrides, ground floor distinct, vertical cores (stairs via the stairs generator, elevator shaft with doors on each floor) aligned across storeys, roof level (parapet/roof access). Each storey is a node with tags so engines can stream per floor.

title: Milestone M1: furnished hotel room (bedroom + ensuite), rendered and exported
description: End-to-end demo: a floor plan with a hotel bedroom and bathroom, interior door, window, finishes, furniture placed by the room archetype solver. Renders cleanly from inside (viewer section view) and exports to GLB with gameplay metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Bedroom + ensuite generated from floor plan + room archetype, rendered via -r, exported with metadata, and walkable in the Godot runtime (collide with walls/furniture, walk through the door)

title: Declarative room archetypes + furnishing solver
description: room_types/*.yaml declare contents as rules instead of coordinates, e.g. hotel_bedroom: bed {against: wall, prefer: longest_wall_not_door, facing: into_room}, nightstand {flank: bed, count: 2}, desk {against: wall, prefer: window_wall}, tv {facing: bed, against: opposite_wall}, wardrobe {near: door}, rug {under: bed}. Solver places items deterministically by seed inside FloorPlan rooms, avoiding door swings, windows and each other, with priorities and optional items; reports unsatisfied rules clearly. Rooms reference a type; floor plans get furnished automatically.
design: Start with a greedy rule-ordered placer on a 2D occupancy grid (walls, door arcs, window zones), candidate positions along walls/relative anchors, score by preferences, backtrack a little. Keep constraints small and composable: against, facing, flank, near, under, centered, clearance, count, optional, priority.

title: Interior material pack: fabric, carpet, tile, marble, chrome, mirror, painted colours
description: Procedural textures: woven fabric (tint param), cut-pile carpet, ceramic/porcelain tile with grout grid (tile size in metres), marble veining, chrome and mirror (high metallic, low roughness), painted plaster in a palette, laminate. Transparency for shower glass/windows lives in o3s.22.
notes: Opaque materials don't need o3s.22; shower glass/window transparency will come with it.

title: Furniture library: hotel bedroom and bathroom
description: Parametric assets with semantic attachments/surfaces and footprint + clearance metadata: bed (frame, mattress, duvet, pillows, headboard), nightstand with drawer, wardrobe, desk + chair, armchair, floor/table lamps, TV + console, luggage rack, mirror, curtains, rug, wall art; bathroom: toilet, vanity + basin + tap, shower (tray, glass screen) and bathtub, towel rail. Soft goods (pillows, cushions, duvet) via subdivision/displacement. Every asset declares tags (e.g. furniture.bed) and footprint so solvers and colliders can use it.
notes: Hard furniture first; soft goods (pillows, duvet, cushions) get upgraded once subdivision (geogen-o3s.14) lands — use rounded boxes/ellipsoids until then.

title: Interior finishes: skirting, cornices, per-room surface materials, light fixtures
description: Skirting boards and crown molding swept along each room's perimeter (broken at door openings), per-room floor/wall/ceiling materials from the room type, ceiling light fixtures and switches at door latch sides. Uses the sweep generator.

title: Interior doors and openings between rooms
description: Doors on shared walls: frame/architrave on both faces, reveals, swing side and direction, leaf as a separate child node with a pivot at the hinge (prepares for articulation). Openings are cut through the correct wall segment via cut_host. Record a door-swing clearance arc in room metadata so furnishing avoids it. Also archways/pass-throughs and exterior entrance doors.

title: Floor plan model + wall generator (shared walls, clean junctions)
description: A FloorPlan describes rooms as polygons (start with axis-aligned rectangles on a grid) plus openings on their edges. Walls are generated once per boundary segment: shared interior walls (e.g. 0.12 m) vs exterior walls (0.3 m), clean L/T/X junctions with no overlap or gaps, floor/ceiling slabs per room. Each room becomes a SceneNode with named surfaces (floor, ceiling, wall segments with side info) and tags (room id/type). YAML: floorplan: {grid: 0.1, rooms: {bedroom: {rect: [x, z, w, d], type: hotel_bedroom}, ...}, doors: [...], windows: [...]}. Supersedes RoomGenerator for multi-room use and fixes corner overlaps.
acceptance_criteria: Two-room + corridor plan renders with no wall overlaps (CSG union watertight), rooms expose floor/wall surfaces, QA tests pass

title: Prototype world: furnished hotel, enterable city, interactive objects
description:
Goal: geogen as a prototype-asset tool for game developers. Generate a reasonable hotel (lobby, corridors, bedrooms, bathrooms, restaurant) populated with typical furniture; a city whose buildings the player can enter; and interactive objects described declaratively (doors, drawers, switches, seats) that export in an engine-agnostic form.

Milestones (task beads, gated by dependencies):
  M1 furnished hotel room -> M2 hotel building -> M3 city district with enterable buildings; M4 interactive objects runs in parallel after gameplay metadata.

Layering: FloorPlan (rooms/walls/openings) -> Building (storeys, cores, facade) -> City (streets, blocks, lots, zoning). Room contents come from declarative room archetypes + a placement solver, not hand-placed coordinates. Gameplay data (colliders, volumes, interactions) rides along as glTF node extras + a JSON sidecar.
design: Principles: (1) everything declarative YAML with seeds for determinism; (2) semantic over coordinates (rooms, walls, 'against longest wall', 'flank bed'); (3) every generated thing carries semantic tags so gameplay metadata falls out for free; (4) engine-agnostic export (glTF extras + JSON schema), with thin engine importers later.
notes: Runtime: Godot 4 is the reference player (decision geogen-3cc.24). Qt viewer stays as the generator inspector; Three.js preview (geogen-3cc.31) and Unity importer (geogen-3cc.22) are later targets.

title: Interactive viewer: easier and more capable
description: User request. Improve the Qt viewer (qt_viewer.py): scene search/filter, frame-selected/reset camera (F/R keys), view presets (front/side/top/iso), wireframe/normals/UV-checker toggles, shadows and shared PBR shading with the offscreen renderer, node selection highlighting with stats (verts/faces/validation), hot-reload of YAML on file change, screenshot/export buttons, WASD/pan controls, grid+axes.
close_reason: New viewer: orbit camera w/ auto-frame + zoom-to-cursor, view presets, shadows, ground, grid/axes, lit/clay/normals/UV-checker modes, wireframe, picking + tree sync + inspector w/ mesh validation, scene filter, hot reload, screenshot, --viewer-screenshot CLI

title: Export: glTF/GLB with PBR materials, and OBJ
description: There is no way to get assets out for a game engine. Export a SceneNode hierarchy to GLB (node hierarchy preserved, PBR metallic-roughness with baked texture images, normal maps, tangents) and OBJ+MTL. CLI: geogen -s X --export out.glb.
close_reason: geogen/export.py: GLB/glTF with node hierarchy + PBR textures (shared Material.gltf_images), OBJ+MTL; CLI -e/--export; round-trip tests

title: Lathe/revolve generator
description: primitive: lathe. Revolve a 2D (r, y) profile around Y with N segments, optional partial sweep angle, crease-aware normals, cylindrical UVs. Enables turned table/chair legs, vases, balusters, lamp posts, bottles, bowls.
close_reason: core/profile.py (shapes, fillets, splines, offsets, earcut triangulation), generators/profiles.py (ExtrudeGenerator, LatheGenerator), YAML primitives extrude/lathe/ellipsoid; table & chair remodeled with turned legs, filleted tops, spindle back, apron clipping fixed

title: Extrude generator (polygon with holes, optional edge bevel)
description: primitive: extrude. Extrude a 2D profile (with holes) along an axis with caps, optional chamfer/round bevel on cap edges, metric UVs, hard-edge normals. Use for tabletops, panels, window frames, trim, signs.
close_reason: core/profile.py (shapes, fillets, splines, offsets, earcut triangulation), generators/profiles.py (ExtrudeGenerator, LatheGenerator), YAML primitives extrude/lathe/ellipsoid; table & chair remodeled with turned legs, filleted tops, spindle back, apron clipping fixed

title: 2D profile toolkit: polylines, arcs, rounded corners, offset, triangulation with holes
description: Foundation for extrude/lathe/sweep. geogen/geometry2d/ (or core/profile.py): Profile/Shape classes, primitives (rect, rounded rect, circle, polygon, arc, bezier), fillet corners, inset/offset, triangulation with holes (trimesh/earcut/shapely), and YAML-friendly construction.
close_reason: core/profile.py (shapes, fillets, splines, offsets, earcut triangulation), generators/profiles.py (ExtrudeGenerator, LatheGenerator), YAML primitives extrude/lathe/ellipsoid; table & chair remodeled with turned legs, filleted tops, spindle back, apron clipping fixed

title: Mesh processing toolkit: weld, crease-angle normals, tangents, validation
description: Mesh has no utilities beyond transform/merge (and merge drops materials). Add geogen/core/meshops.py: weld_vertices(tol), compute_normals(crease_angle) (smooth within angle, split across hard edges), compute_tangents (for normal maps), validate() reporting degenerate faces, non-manifold edges, open boundaries, inconsistent winding. Generators should emit explicit normals.
close_reason: Implemented: render.py (shadows, PBR maps, --views contact sheet), rounded box replaces broken bevel winding, core/meshops.py with tests

title: Metric UV mapping (box/planar/cylindrical projection, texels per metre)
description: Primitives emit 0-1 UVs per face, so texture density depends on object size (bricks stretch differently on each wall, roofs vs chimney). Add UV projection helpers (box/triplanar-style per-face, planar, cylindrical) parameterised by world units per texture tile, and make generators use metric UVs by default so a brick is the same size everywhere.
close_reason: Metric UVs in all primitives + rooms (core/uvmap.py box/planar/cylindrical), Material.tile_size in metres, renderer+Qt viewer honour it

title: Beveled cube edges render as bright white seams
description: Every beveled cube (chairs, table, house) shows white lines along bevel strips in renders. Likely bevel strip/corner UVs are degenerate (constant v) so they sample the texture edge row, or normals are missing and trimesh averages them. Fix so bevels shade continuous with faces.
close_reason: Implemented: render.py (shadows, PBR maps, --views contact sheet), rounded box replaces broken bevel winding, core/meshops.py with tests

title: Offscreen render quality: shadows, PBR maps, multi-view contact sheet
description: The -r render path (main.py) uses pyrender with no shadows, ignores normal/roughness maps, and renders one fixed view. Judging geometry quality requires: directional shadows, material PBR maps passed through, and a --views option producing a front/side/top/iso contact sheet in one PNG. Extract rendering out of main.py into geogen/render.py so tests and tools can reuse it.
acceptance_criteria: geogen -s X -r out.png --views produces a 2x2 contact sheet with shadows; render code lives in geogen/render.py
close_reason: Implemented: render.py (shadows, PBR maps, --views contact sheet), rounded box replaces broken bevel winding, core/meshops.py with tests

title: High-quality procedural geometry
description: Umbrella for moving geogen from box/cylinder primitives to production-quality procedural geometry for scenery and interiors: solid mesh foundation (normals, UVs, validation), richer modeling operations (extrude/lathe/sweep/booleans/fillets/subdivision), domain generators (roofs, walls with openings, stairs, trees), export (glTF/OBJ, LOD), and a render loop good enough to judge quality.

title: Godot chunk streaming for large scenes
description: Load city/building exports by manifest: stream exterior chunks by distance, use exported LODs/visibility ranges, load building interiors when the player approaches an entrance or enters a lot, unload behind. Background loading via ResourceLoader threaded requests so walking stays smooth.

title: Headless Godot playtest in CI (enterability checks)
description: Run Godot headless in CI on exported scenes: import, bake/load navmesh, spawn the player capsule at each spawn point, and assert every room volume and every interaction point is reachable via NavigationServer3D paths; walk a scripted bot along the path to catch step/slope/door-width problems that 2D validation misses. Report failures with room/part names. Complements 3cc.8 (generator-side validation).

title: Godot interaction runtime for geogen components
description: Godot implementation of the declarative interaction vocabulary from 3cc.19: openable (animate hinge/slide pivot between named states, locked + key id, auto-close), container (drawers/wardrobes, simple inventory), switchable (toggle a light group + emissive materials), seat/bed (move player camera to sit/lie point with facing), usable (TV on/off, tap, elevator call). Player interaction: centre-screen raycast within reach, prompt label, E to use. States serialisable so a level can save/restore. Each component is a script the import plugin attaches from extras.geogen.interactions.

title: Milestone M4: interactive hotel room
description: The M1 room with working declarative interactions: openable/lockable doors, wardrobe and nightstand drawers, light switch controlling ceiling light and lamps, sit on chair, lie on bed. Previewable in the viewer and exported for an engine.
acceptance_criteria: In Godot: open/lock the room door, open wardrobe and nightstand drawers, toggle lights from the switch, sit on the chair, lie on the bed

title: Viewer (inspector): section/cutaway, storey selector, interaction state preview
description: Generator-side inspection in the Qt viewer: clip plane / hide roof and upper storeys, storey selector for multi-floor buildings, show tags, room volumes, colliders and interaction components in the inspector, and scrub joint states (door open/closed) to check pivots. First-person walking lives in the Godot runtime, not here.

title: Lighting as content: fixtures, emissive, exported lights
description: Light fixtures carry a light (point/spot/area-ish) plus emissive bulb/shade materials; exported via KHR_lights_punctual; switch groups for interactions. Viewer supports many lights (nearest-N per mesh or clustered) instead of the current 4, and a night mode for interiors.

title: Declarative interaction components
description: interactions: block on assets, engine-agnostic: openable (uses a joint, locked flag, auto-close), container (drawer/wardrobe with capacity), switchable (light switch toggles a named light/emissive group), seat (sit point + facing), bed (lie point), usable (tap, TV, elevator call button with target). States + transitions declared in data; exported via extras + sidecar schema. Room archetypes can attach interactions, e.g. every hotel door openable+lockable with a key id.

title: Articulated parts: hinge and slide joints
description: Declare joints in asset YAML: joint: {type: hinge, axis: y, pivot: left_edge, limits: [0, 100]} or {type: slide, axis: z, range: [0, 0.4]}. The loader re-parents the moving part under a pivot node so its transform is the joint state. Named states (closed/open). Export pivots so engines can animate; optional glTF animations per state transition.

title: Scale: instancing, caching, chunked export, exterior LODs
description: A city has thousands of repeated meshes: share Mesh objects between identical asset instances (hash params+seed), reuse meshes in glTF, cache generated assets on disk, export per building/block chunks with a manifest, exterior LODs for distant buildings, and interior-on-demand so engines can stream interiors when entered.

title: Building type catalogue + lot fitting
description: Parametric recipes: hotel, apartment block, shop row (ground-floor retail + flats above), office, detached house. Each fits a lot (setbacks, footprint within lot, entrance facing the street, height by zone) and decides which interiors are generated (full, lobby-only, or closed shell for background buildings).

title: City layout: street grid, blocks, lots, zoning
description: Start with a grid street network (parameters: block size, street widths, avenue spacing); roads with curbs, sidewalks, crosswalks and intersections; blocks subdivided into lots; zoning assigns building types per lot (commercial main street, residential, hotel/landmark). Street furniture scattered along sidewalks (lamps, trees, benches, hydrants).
notes: Streets/sidewalks export walkable navmesh nodes (-navmesh) for the Godot runtime.

title: Milestone M2: hotel building (lobby + N guest floors), enterable
description: A generated hotel: lobby level with reception/restaurant, several guest floors of furnished rooms via archetypes, stairs and elevator, facade and roof. Player-scale correct, exported with colliders and room volumes, explorable in the viewer's walk mode.
acceptance_criteria: Hotel exported and explorable in Godot: lobby, stairs/elevator to guest floors, enterable rooms; headless playtest passes

title: Facade generator driven by the floor plan
description: Exterior generated from the building: windows where rooms have exterior windows (rhythmic bays), balconies, ground-floor entrance canopy or storefront glazing, floor bands and cornices, parapet/roof. Style presets (brick hotel, stucco, modern curtain wall) selectable by parameter.

title: Procedural floor plan layouts (hotel corridor floors, lobby level)
description: Generate FloorPlans from a footprint + program instead of hand-authoring: double-loaded corridor (rooms both sides, core in the middle, fire stairs at the ends) with a room module width; lobby/ground floor program (entrance, reception, lounge, restaurant, restrooms, back-of-house). Parametric: footprint size, corridor width, room module, ensuite on/off.

title: Layout validation: overlaps, door clearance, navigability
description: QA checks for generated interiors: furniture-furniture and furniture-wall intersection (bounding boxes then mesh), door swing arcs clear, window access, and navigability via a 2D occupancy grid path from room entrance to every interaction point (bed side, desk chair, toilet). Runs in tests and shows problems in the viewer inspector.
notes: Use the shared player spec (player.yaml) for clearances, corridor/door widths and step/slope limits.

title: Remodel houses with roof and wall/opening generators
description: Rebuild house_simple/house_peaked with real roofs (closed gables, overhang, fascia), walls with cut openings, framed windows and panelled doors, trim.
close_reason: house_peaked rebuilt (hollow shell, gable roof, gables, chimney) + cottage scene with cut openings; street uses cottages. house_simple (flat roof) left as-is, now unused by street.

title: Remodel furniture with new generators (turned legs, rounded tops, fix table apron clipping)
description: Chair/table use raw boxes and the table apron pokes through the tabletop. Rebuild with lathe legs, rounded-box/extruded tops, proper joinery offsets, and a cushioned seat option.
close_reason: Table & chair remodeled with lathe legs/spindles, filleted extruded tops, apron clipping fixed

title: Geometry QA test suite across all assets
description: Parametrised pytest over every asset/scene: no degenerate faces, no NaNs, normals present and unit length, outward winding for closed parts, UVs present, texel density within bounds, bounding box matches declared size.
close_reason: tests/test_asset_quality.py: validity, metric UVs, non-empty, declared-size fit across all registry scenes

title: Roof generator: gable, hip, shed with overhang, fascia, closed gables
description: house_peaked builds a roof from two rotated cubes, leaving open triangular gable ends and a float-precision seam at the ridge. Add primitive: roof with types gable/hip/shed/flat, pitch, overhang, thickness, fascia board, ridge cap, and gable wall fill piece.
close_reason: core/csg.py (manifold3d, UV-preserving); YAML subtract/cutter and cut_host (placed windows/doors cut openings in the host wall via Surface.source); generators/architecture.py RoofGenerator (gable/hip/shed/flat, overhang, ridge cap, face-planar UVs) + PrismGenerator; window.yaml/door.yaml assets; house_peaked rebuilt as hollow shell; scenes/cottage.yaml; street house plots now use cottages

title: Wall-with-openings generator: windows and doors with frames, mullions, glass, sills
description: Houses currently paste flat boxes on walls. Generate walls with real openings (thickness, reveals), window assemblies (frame profile, mullions/muntins grid, glass pane, sill, lintel) and doors (panelled leaf, frame, handle). Parametric via YAML.
close_reason: core/csg.py (manifold3d, UV-preserving); YAML subtract/cutter and cut_host (placed windows/doors cut openings in the host wall via Surface.source); generators/architecture.py RoofGenerator (gable/hip/shed/flat, overhang, ridge cap, face-planar UVs) + PrismGenerator; window.yaml/door.yaml assets; house_peaked rebuilt as hollow shell; scenes/cottage.yaml; street house plots now use cottages

title: CSG booleans via manifold3d
description: Add union/difference/intersection on Mesh via manifold3d (optional dependency, robust). Exposed in YAML (e.g. part subtract: [other_part]) for cut-outs such as window openings, sink holes, arches.
close_reason: core/csg.py (manifold3d, UV-preserving); YAML subtract/cutter and cut_host (placed windows/doors cut openings in the host wall via Surface.source); generators/architecture.py RoofGenerator (gable/hip/shed/flat, overhang, ridge cap, face-planar UVs) + PrismGenerator; window.yaml/door.yaml assets; house_peaked rebuilt as hollow shell; scenes/cottage.yaml; street house plots now use cottages

title: Rounded box, ellipsoid, torus, capsule primitives
description: Current bevel is a single chamfer; sphere uses min(size) so it cannot be an ellipsoid. Add rounded_box (fillet radius + segments, smooth normals), true ellipsoid scaling for sphere, torus, capsule, and cylinder/cone with bevelled rims.
notes: Done: rounded box (cube bevel+bevel_segments), ellipsoid primitive. Remaining: torus, capsule, beveled cylinder rims (lathe can cover these via profiles).

title: Sweep generator: profile along 3D path
description: primitive: sweep. Sweep a 2D profile along a polyline/bezier path using rotation-minimising frames, with optional caps and scale/twist along path. Use for pipes, railings, cables, crown moldings, baseboards, tree branches, road curbs.

title: Three.js web preview runtime (same schema subset)
description: Lightweight, shareable browser preview of exported GLBs: orbit + simple walk mode, room/tag inspector, toggle openable/switchable components from extras.geogen. Proves the schema is engine-agnostic and gives a no-install way to share generated buildings. Not a full game runtime.

title: Unity importer for geogen exports (glTFast + extras.geogen)
description: Later engine target: Unity import pipeline reading glTF extras.geogen (custom glTFast import add-on), creating colliders from the naming convention, trigger volumes, spawns, and MonoBehaviours for the interaction components. Godot remains the reference implementation (see decision bead).

title: Milestone M3: city district with enterable buildings
description: A few blocks with streets, mixed building types from the catalogue, at least the hotel and shops enterable with furnished interiors, background buildings as shells. Exported in chunks with a manifest; walkable in the viewer.
acceptance_criteria: District exported in chunks with a manifest; Godot streams it and the player can walk streets and enter the hotel and shops

title: Assets declare sizes that don't match their geometry
description: maple_tree, pine_tree, street_lamp use size [scale,scale,scale]=1m but are 1.7-4.8m tall; fire_hydrant declares width 0.3 but outlets make it 0.51 wide. Declared size drives anchors, attachments and framing, so these should declare their true bounds (e.g. a 'scale' param multiplying a real size). Listed in KNOWN_SIZE_MISMATCH in tests/test_asset_quality.py; remove entries as fixed.

title: Wood material: reduce harsh specular hotspot
description: Tabletop renders show a strong sun hotspot in top view. Tune wood roughness map/normalisation in render.py and wood.yaml so varnished wood reads softer.

title: Room walls overlap/stick out at corners
description: In the room scene render, the east wall extends past the adjoining walls at the corner (visible as a protruding slab in iso view). Wall panels should miter or butt cleanly.
notes: Will be resolved by the FloorPlan wall generator (geogen-3cc.1); close when rooms use it.

title: Materials: glass/transparency, emissive, vertex colors, per-face material groups
description: Windows need glass, lamps need emissive, and multi-material meshes need material groups. Extend Material and viewer/renderer/exporter.
notes: glass, trim_white, door_paint materials added (opaque glass approximation: dark, low roughness, metallic 0.6). Remaining: true transparency/alpha, emissive (lamps), vertex colours, multi-material meshes.

title: Seeded variation and scatter placement (Poisson disk, along paths, on surfaces)
description: Scenes are hand-placed. Add seeded param randomisation (ranges in YAML) and scatter placements: Poisson-disk in region, along path with spacing, on surface with density map, with collision avoidance.

title: Procedural trees and rocks
description: Trees are spheres on cylinders. Build branch skeletons (space colonisation or L-system), sweep branches with tapering, leaf cards/clusters; rocks from displaced subdivided cages.

title: LOD generation via mesh decimation
description: Generate LOD chains (e.g. 100/50/25%) with quadric decimation preserving UV seams and hard edges; export as glTF LOD nodes. Also parametric LOD: generators accept a detail level (segments).

title: Subdivision surfaces (Catmull-Clark/Loop) and displacement
description: Smooth organic forms: subdivide a coarse cage with crease support, plus noise displacement along normals. Use for rocks, cushions, foliage clumps, terrain features.

title: Stairs generator (straight, L, spiral) with railings
description: Parametric stairs: rise/run/width, stringers, treads with nosing, optional railings via sweep. Needed for interiors and multi-storey buildings.
